headline: Target comps fall 2.7% as traffic drops 2.2%; discretionary stays pressured and FY profit outlook trimmed.
guidance_note: FY25 adj EPS narrowed to ~$7.00-8.00 (GAAP ~$7.70-8.70), lowering the midpoint; Q4 low-single-digit sales decline maintained.
key_messages: Comps -2.7% (stores -3.8%, digital +2.4%); transactions -2.2% and average ticket -0.5%.
Food & beverage and hardlines comped positive while discretionary categories stayed under pressure.
Gross margin 28.2% vs 28.3% on higher markdowns, offset by ads, lower shrink and supply-chain efficiency.
Adjusted EPS $1.78 vs $1.85, modestly above consensus; GAAP $1.51 after severance and asset charges.

consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary categories remained pressured as consumers prioritized value and necessity.

macro_read: Late-2025 shoppers at Target bought essentials but held back on discretionary goods, consistent with a value-focused, selective consumer rather than a broad pullback.

sources.label: Nasdaq/Zacks: Q3 sales decline amid soft traffic
